steps.intent: France seeks a firm Council response that condemns the reported chemical weapons attack, supports an OPCW/JIM investigation, and keeps accountability on the table while avoiding explicit attribution or coercive Chapter VII measures that would invite a Russian veto. The main difficulties will be Russian objections to any language implying Syrian government responsibility, the reference to the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and demands for access and reporting timelines; some Council members may also press for stronger attribution or sanctions. We will negotiate on the basis of the "reported attack," full OPCW cooperation, and a clear reporting deadline to secure at least nine votes without a veto.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia condemns all use of chemical weapons, but cannot support a one-sided draft that prejudges responsibility and ignores the 7 April unilateral missile strike. We request balanced language affirming respect for Syrian sovereignty, rejecting unilateral military action, and conditioning condemnation on impartial OPCW confirmation. The text must also reaffirm that only a Syrian-led political solution can end the conflict.
messages.China: China condemns any use of chemical weapons and supports a thorough, impartial and professional investigation by the OPCW and the JIM. The current text must not prejudge responsibility before the investigation; references to Khan Shaykhun and accountability should be tied to verified findings. China also asks that cooperation be set in the framework of respect for Syria's sovereignty and that the Council oppose unilateral military action. If these concerns are not reflected, China cannot support the draft.
messages.Egypt: Egypt supports the draft’s core objective of condemning chemical weapons use and ensuring accountability. We ask that the text avoid prejudging responsibility and require an impartial, objective and non-politicized investigation. We also ask that cooperation obligations explicitly cover armed groups and terrorist organizations, consistent with Egypt’s long-standing concerns about non-State actors and chemical weapons.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia firmly condemns any use of chemical weapons and supports an impartial OPCW/JIM-led investigation. To support the text, we need OP1 to avoid prejudging the outcome and a new paragraph reaffirming Syria's sovereignty and calling on all States to de-escalate. We also believe the draft should recall the political track under resolution 2254.
messages.Italy: Italy supports the draft as circulated. We strongly condemn the reported chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun and believe the Council must speak with one voice on accountability, full OPCW and JIM cooperation, and access to all relevant sites. We therefore support the current text and urge all members to adopt it without weakening its core provisions.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the draft as circulated. We strongly condemn the reported chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun and believe the Council must send a clear message that any use of chemical weapons is unacceptable and that those responsible must be held accountable. The text appropriately calls for full cooperation with the OPCW and the JIM, including immediate, safe and unhindered access. Japan urges all Council members to support the draft so that the Council can act without delay.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan strongly condemns any use of chemical weapons and supports a thorough OPCW/JIM investigation. We can support this draft if OP1 does not prejudge responsibility and if the Council explicitly bases any further action on the OPCW/JIM reports, with full respect for Syria's sovereignty and the UN Charter. We also seek balanced language requiring all parties, including non-State armed groups, to cooperate. Without these changes we would have to abstain.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support this draft as it stands. We insist on removing any pre-judgment of responsibility and on ensuring that the call to cooperate is addressed to all parties, not only the Syrian Government. We also require a clear reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty and a balanced reference to unilateral military actions. If these red lines are reflected, we are prepared to continue working; otherwise we will not support the text.
messages.Senegal: Senegal supports the draft as circulated. The use of chemical weapons is unacceptable and cannot be justified under any circumstances, and the Council must speak clearly and ensure a swift, impartial investigation and accountability. We see no need for changes at this stage and urge the Council to proceed to a vote.
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports this draft and the Council’s clear message against chemical weapons. We ask that OP4 explicitly require Syria to ensure the safety and security of OPCW and JIM personnel, and that a new operative paragraph demand immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and protection of medical and humanitarian personnel. Sweden will vote in favour and urges all members to do so.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine supports the draft as presented. It provides a balanced and firm response to the Khan Shaykhun chemical attack and preserves the central role of the OPCW and the JIM. We see no need for amendments and urge the Council to adopt it without delay.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports this draft as a basis and welcomes France’s penhold. We need the Council to condemn the Khan Shaykhun attack in the strongest terms, not merely as a 'reported attack', and to demand that Syria provide immediate access to Shayrat airbase and flight data. We also want an explicit intention to return with further measures if Syria does not comply; these points are essential for accountability and for the credibility of the Council.
messages.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor and supports the draft as written. It delivers a clear condemnation, demands Syrian cooperation with the OPCW and JIM, and preserves accountability. We urge all members to join us in adopting it without weakening its core provisions.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay thanks the penholders and supports the draft. We would like the Council to condemn the attack in the strongest terms, to include an operative demand for immediate humanitarian access throughout Syria, and to make clear that the JIM's findings must lead to accountability, including through Council action. These changes would strengthen a text that Uruguay can support.

steps.summary: France revised the draft to strengthen condemnation and accountability, include humanitarian access, and partially address calls for all-party cooperation and sovereignty. Core red lines of Russia and Bolivia on pre-judgment and unilateral action were rejected, so the revised text is expected to face a Russian veto despite broad support.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): The current text remains unbalanced: it prejudges the Khan Shaykhun incident before the OPCW has reported and ignores the US missile strike against Shayrat, which violates Syrian sovereignty. Bolivia cannot support a draft that singles out Syria, threatens sanctions, and fails to reaffirm the Charter's prohibition on the use or threat of force. We maintain our red lines on an explicit reference to the 7 April strike, language preserving an impartial investigation, and deletion of the sanctions threat. We are ready to engage constructively on a balanced text that upholds sovereignty, non-intervention, and a political solution.
messages.China: China supports the Council's unity against chemical weapons and an impartial OPCW/JIM investigation. However, the current text still prejudges the Khan Shaykhun incident and contains a sanctions threat that China cannot accept, while failing to reject unilateral military action. Unless OP1 and OP12 are revised and a clear clause on sovereignty and unilateral action is added, China will abstain.
messages.Egypt: Egypt condemns any use of chemical weapons and supports a thorough investigation, but the current text must not prejudge responsibility or threaten sanctions before the OPCW and JIM establish the facts. We therefore ask that OP12 be revised to remove the sanctions threat and the singling out of Syria, and that OP1 and OP9 reflect an impartial, objective and non-politicized process. Egypt can support the draft if these concerns are met.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia has a firm and uncompromising position against chemical weapons and supports a thorough, impartial OPCW/JIM investigation. However, the current OP1 prejudges the outcome before the OPCW has confirmed the facts, which we cannot accept. Unless OP1 is revised to reflect the pending investigation, Ethiopia will abstain.
messages.Italy: Italy supports the current text as a balanced and necessary response to the Khan Shaykhun chemical attack and will vote in favour. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons and insist on full, immediate and unhindered OPCW and JIM access, including to Shayrat airbase and relevant records. The text appropriately reaffirms Syrian sovereignty and the centrality of a political solution under resolution 2254 (2015), and we urge all Council members to speak with one voice on accountability and humanitarian access.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current draft as a necessary and balanced response to the Khan Shaykhun chemical weapons attack. We welcome its clear condemnation, its demand for full Syrian cooperation with the OPCW and JIM, including access and flight records, and its emphasis on accountability and humanitarian access. Japan urges all Council members to unite behind this text so that the Council sends an unequivocal message that chemical weapons use is unacceptable under any circumstances.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan appreciates the inclusion of non-State armed groups in OP6 and remains committed to accountability for chemical weapons use. However, OP1 still prejudges responsibility before the OPCW and JIM have reported, and OP12’s explicit sanctions threat, particularly against Syria, is premature and could undermine the political process. We therefore cannot support the current text and will abstain unless OP1 is made neutral and OP12 is revised to defer Council action until the investigation reports are reviewed.
messages.Russian Federation: The current draft remains unacceptable: it prejudges responsibility, singles out Syria, and threatens sanctions, all of which are red lines for the Russian Federation. We cannot support this text and will vote against it unless OP1, OP5 and OP12 are revised as set out. The Council must also address unilateral military action against Syria rather than legitimizing it.
messages.Senegal: Senegal supports the current draft. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons and believe the OPCW and JIM must be allowed to investigate and establish accountability. The text rightly demands humanitarian access and reaffirms that only a political solution can end the conflict. Senegal will vote in favour of the draft as it stands and urges the Council to remain united.
messages.Sweden: Sweden supports the draft and welcomes the inclusion of humanitarian access and safety for OPCW and JIM personnel. We ask that OP7 explicitly protect medical and humanitarian facilities as well as personnel, consistent with resolution 2286 (2016). With that amendment, Sweden is ready to vote in favour.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine supports the draft as revised. It properly condemns the Khan Shaykhun chemical weapons attack, demands full cooperation by the Syrian Arab Republic with the OPCW and JIM, including access to Shayrat airbase and flight records, and preserves accountability and humanitarian access. We see no need for changes and call for its swift adoption.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the current draft and is proud to co-sponsor it. The revised OP1, OP5 and OP12 meet our core objectives: condemning the Khan Shaykhun attack in the strongest terms, demanding full access to Shayrat and flight records, and signalling further measures for non-compliance. We urge the penholder to move to a vote without further weakening, and call on all Council members to support the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the revised draft as a co-sponsor. It clearly condemns the Khan Shaykhun chemical weapons attack, demands Syrian cooperation with the OPCW and JIM, and preserves accountability and the option of further measures. We urge all Council members to adopt it without delay and oppose any weakening of OPs 5, 9, or 11.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay welcomes the revisions made in response to our earlier requests, particularly the strengthened condemnation, the humanitarian access provision, and the clear link between JIM findings and Council action. The text as revised reflects a balanced and credible response to the Khan Shaykhun attack while reaffirming Syrian sovereignty and the need to avoid further escalation. We support the draft and urge the Council to speak with one voice on accountability and full cooperation with the OPCW and the JIM.

steps.summary: France retained the core condemnation, OPCW/JIM access including Shayrat, and a further-measures option while accepting technical improvements on facilities and impartiality. The text is expected to receive 10 votes in favour, with Russia and Bolivia opposing; Russia's negative vote vetoes the draft. China, Ethiopia, and Kazakhstan are expected to abstain.

reasons.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia had already opposed the draft and its red-line amendments were rejected; its anti-interventionist foreign policy and rejection of the US strike and sanctions threats make a “No” vote the consistent choice.
reasons.China: China’s core requested changes—removing pre-judgment of responsibility and deleting the sanctions threat in OP12—were rejected, so abstention follows its record and avoids a veto while preserving support for impartial investigation and political settlement.
reasons.Egypt: Egypt supported the draft in the real vote: it condemns chemical weapons use and mandates investigation while Egypt voices reservations about politicization and sanctions conditionality. A favourable vote aligns with its stated support-with-changes posture and regional interest in accountability without prejudging responsibility.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia’s stated red line was the replacement of OP1 with language referring to the Khan Shaykhun attack as reported pending OPCW confirmation; the penholder rejected it. Consistent with its prior abstention on the February Syria chemical-weapons draft and its emphasis on impartial investigation and sovereignty, Ethiopia abstains.
reasons.France: France is the lead sponsor of the draft and has consistently supported strong Council action on chemical weapons and accountability in Syria. It would therefore speak in favour and vote yes.
reasons.Italy: Italy has consistently supported accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria and voted in favour of the earlier France-UK-US draft, so it supports this text without requesting changes. Speaking before the vote reinforces Italy’s support for OPCW/JIM investigations, humanitarian access, and a unified Council response.
reasons.Japan: Japan consistently supports accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria and voted in favour of prior OPCW/JIM-related drafts. The draft aligns with Japan’s stated position on upholding the chemical weapons norm and humanitarian access.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan’s red-line request on OP1 and important request on OP12 were rejected, and its prior position on chemical-weapons accountability was to abstain when the text prejudged responsibility or moved toward sanctions before impartial investigation. Abstention matches its balancing posture: strong opposition to chemical weapons plus defense of sovereignty and non-politicized OPCW/JIM findings.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia opposes the draft because it prejudges the Khan Shaykhun investigation, maintains Syria-specific demands, and includes a sanctions threat; Moscow will veto to protect Syrian sovereignty and reject a politicized text.
reasons.Senegal: Senegal has consistently voted in favour of Council action on chemical weapons accountability in Syria, including the February 2017 draft, and its stated policy condemns chemical weapons while stressing sovereignty, humanitarian access and a political solution. The draft aligns with those priorities and Senegal had already signalled support without requesting changes.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden’s priority is accountability for chemical weapons use and humanitarian protection in Syria; its requested OP7 change was accepted, and the draft aligns with its support for the OPCW/JIM and international law.
reasons.Ukraine: Ukraine consistently supports chemical-weapons accountability and OPCW/JIM investigations, and it aligns with the Western-supported draft against Russian opposition. Kyiv would vote in favour while emphasizing sovereignty and humanitarian access.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK co-sponsored the draft and consistently supports accountability for chemical weapons use in Syria, strong OPCW/JIM access, and further measures in the event of non-compliance. Speaking before the vote reinforces UK leadership and pressure on Council members to support the resolution.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor and strongly supports condemnation of the Khan Shaykhun chemical attack, OPCW/JIM investigations, and accountability. It would speak before the vote to press all Council members, especially Russia, to support the resolution.
reasons.Uruguay: Uruguay has consistently supported accountability for chemical weapons use and humanitarian access in Syria, and its last negotiation position was support without requested changes. The draft is consistent with Uruguay’s principled position against impunity and for a UN-led political solution.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): The delegation of the Plurinational State of Bolivia will vote against this draft resolution. Bolivia unequivocally condemns the use of chemical weapons by any actor in Syria and supports a transparent, independent and impartial investigation by the OPCW. However, this text is unbalanced and premature: it prejudges the outcome of an ongoing investigation, ignores the grave violation of Syrian sovereignty constituted by the unilateral United States missile strike of 7 April, and opens the door to sanctions against a sovereign State. Bolivia cannot support a draft that deepens confrontation and undermines a political solution, and calls instead for full respect for international law, non-intervention and the territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.
before.China: Mr. President, China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances. We support a comprehensive, impartial and objective investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and we believe that the facts must be established on the basis of reliable evidence and in accordance with professional procedures. The Security Council should act responsibly to maintain unity on the Syrian chemical weapons issue. However, the draft before us still prejudges responsibility before the investigation is completed, and it contains provisions threatening further measures, including sanctions, which are not conducive to a political settlement or to Council unity. China also believes that the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria must be respected and that unilateral military actions must be avoided. For these reasons, China will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.Egypt: Egypt will vote in favour of this draft resolution. My delegation has consistently rejected any use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances, and supports an impartial, objective, transparent and non-politicized investigation so that responsibility is determined on the basis of verified facts. We stress that the implementation of this resolution, including paragraph 12, must be based on the findings of the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism and in full accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, without prejudging the outcome or politicizing the process. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and the JIM, to guarantee safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and to return to a political settlement under United Nations auspices.
before.Ethiopia: Ethiopia has a firm and uncompromising position against the use of chemical weapons, born of our own experience, and we condemn any such use in Syria. We support a swift, independent and impartial investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and we call on all parties to cooperate fully and provide unhindered access. However, the draft before us prejudges the findings of the investigation in its very first operative paragraph and sets the Council on a path toward sanctions before the facts have been established. Ethiopia requested that the text refer to the reported attack in Khan Shaykhun pending confirmation by the OPCW, but that request was not accepted. For that reason, while we strongly support accountability and the protection of civilians, Ethiopia will abstain.
before.France: France votes in favour of this resolution. The chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. The Security Council cannot remain silent in the face of the use of chemical weapons against civilians. This text is balanced and focused: it condemns the attack, demands full cooperation with the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, calls for immediate and unhindered access, and preserves the path toward accountability. France has negotiated in good faith. We call on all members of this Council to unite behind this resolution and to send a clear message that those responsible for chemical weapons use will not enjoy impunity.
before.Italy: Thank you, Mr. President. Italy will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn the appalling chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun on 4 April and express our deepest condolences to the victims and their families. The use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law and cannot go unpunished. Italy fully supports the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism and calls on the Syrian authorities to cooperate immediately, fully and without conditions, including by providing access to Shayrat airbase and all relevant information. Accountability must be established through an independent, impartial and objective investigation. At the same time, we stress the need for immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria and for the protection of civilians and medical and humanitarian personnel. Italy remains convinced that there can be no military solution to this conflict; only a political settlement under United Nations auspices, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), can bring lasting peace while respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We urge all members of the Council to support this text and to uphold the Council’s unity and credibility in the face of grave violations of international law.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn the reported use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun on 4 April 2017. The use of chemical weapons is unacceptable under any circumstances and constitutes a serious violation of international law. It is essential that the Security Council uphold the chemical weapons prohibition, ensure a swift, impartial and thorough investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and hold those responsible accountable. Japan also stresses the need for immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria and for all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and the JIM. We reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and support efforts towards a political solution under United Nations auspices in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Kazakhstan:
Mr. President, Kazakhstan has consistently and unequivocally opposed the use of chemical weapons anywhere and by anyone. Such use is a grave violation of international law and cannot be justified under any circumstances. We express our deep outrage at the loss of civilian life in Khan Shaykhun and support a prompt, impartial, objective and independent investigation by the OPCW and the JIM so that the facts are established and those responsible are held accountable.

At the same time, Kazakhstan regrets that the draft before the Council retains formulations that prejudge responsibility before the investigation has concluded and that envisage further measures, including sanctions, before the Council has received and reviewed the reports of the OPCW and the JIM. We believe the Council must be guided by verified facts, avoid politicization, and respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. A sustainable settlement can only be reached through a political process under United Nations auspices in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).

For these reasons, Kazakhstan will abstain on this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation: Mr President, the Russian Federation will vote against this draft resolution. We are gravely concerned by the reports of the use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun and the loss of civilian life, and we support an impartial and objective investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism. However, this draft is unbalanced and politicized. It prejudges responsibility before an investigation has established the facts, makes selective demands on the Syrian Government while imposing no equivalent requirements on armed groups and terrorist organizations, and contains an unacceptable threat of sanctions. It also fails to condemn unilateral military action against Syria that violates Syrian sovereignty and international law. Our proposed amendments would have made the text balanced and legitimate, but the co-sponsors rejected them. We cannot support a resolution that undermines the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic and creates a dangerous precedent. The Russian Federation therefore votes against.
before.Senegal: Mr. President, Senegal will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and can never be justified. We condemn in the strongest terms the attack in Khan Shaykhun, and we express our deep sorrow at the loss of civilian life. Senegal supports an independent, impartial and transparent investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism. We call on the Syrian authorities and all parties to cooperate fully, grant immediate and unhindered access to relevant sites and information, and preserve evidence so that those responsible can be held accountable. At the same time, we urge all actors to avoid further escalation, to respect the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria, and to renew efforts for unhindered humanitarian access and a political solution under resolution 2254 (2015). Senegal supports this balanced text and remains committed to the unity of the Council in addressing this grave situation.
before.Sweden: Sweden will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The use of chemical weapons is a serious violation of international law and cannot be tolerated. We strongly support an independent, impartial and credible investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and we call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to provide immediate, safe and unhindered access to all relevant sites and information. The Council must be united in upholding accountability and in demanding full respect for international humanitarian law, including the protection of medical and humanitarian personnel and facilities. Sweden therefore urges all members to support this resolution.
before.Ukraine: Ukraine strongly condemns the use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun and any such use anywhere. This is a serious violation of international law and cannot go unpunished. We support an impartial, objective and transparent investigation by the OPCW and the JIM, and we call on the Syrian authorities and all other parties to provide immediate, safe and unhindered access to relevant sites and information. Accountability for chemical weapons use is essential, and Ukraine will vote in favour of this draft resolution. At the same time, we reaffirm Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and stress the urgent need for full humanitarian access and a sustainable political settlement under United Nations auspices.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr President, the United Kingdom co-sponsored this draft resolution because the Security Council cannot remain silent in the face of the chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun. The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. The Syrian regime must provide the OPCW and the JIM with immediate, safe and unhindered access to all relevant sites, including Shayrat airbase, and make available all relevant information, including flight plans, flight logs and records of air operations. This resolution is balanced, factual and focused on accountability. It does not prejudge the investigation, but it makes clear that those responsible must be held accountable. It also rightly demands humanitarian access throughout Syria and reaffirms that only a political solution can end the conflict. The United Kingdom fully supports this text and will vote in favour. We call on all members of the Council to do likewise.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States is a co-sponsor of this resolution because the use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun on 4 April was an atrocity that this Council cannot ignore. Dozens of civilians, including children, were killed in an attack that bears the hallmarks of the Syrian regime’s continued violations of international law and its obligations under resolution 2118 and the Chemical Weapons Convention. This resolution is clear, practical, and necessary: it condemns the attack, demands full cooperation with the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and requires immediate access to Shayrat airbase and all relevant information, including flight logs and records. The United States urges every member of this Council to vote in favour. Let us be clear: this is not about politics; it is about enforcing the global prohibition on chemical weapons and ensuring that those responsible are held accountable. Any member that blocks this text would send a dangerous message that chemical weapons can be used with impunity. The United States will vote yes, and we call on all members to do the same.
before.Uruguay: Uruguay will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The reported use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun is a grave violation of international law and cannot be met with indifference or impunity. We support an impartial, independent and non-politicized investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and we call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully and provide immediate, safe and unhindered access. At the same time, Uruguay reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and stresses that accountability and humanitarian access must serve, not replace, the search for a political solution through intra-Syrian negotiations under United Nations auspices.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China has just abstained on the draft resolution before the Council. China firmly opposes the use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances. We support a comprehensive, impartial and objective investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and we believe that the facts must be established on the basis of reliable evidence and professional procedures.

At the same time, China believes that the draft prejudged responsibility before the investigation was completed and contained provisions threatening further measures, including sanctions. Such an approach is not conducive to maintaining Council unity or to advancing a political settlement. China also believes that the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria must be respected, and that unilateral military actions that violate international law are unacceptable and risk further escalation.

China regrets that the Council could not reach consensus. The Security Council should remain united on the Syrian chemical weapons issue. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and the JIM, provide safe, immediate and unhindered access, and ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches all those in need. Any accountability must be based on the findings of an impartial investigation and in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations. At the same time, the priority must remain a political solution through intra-Syrian negotiations under United Nations auspices in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). China will continue to play a constructive role in this effort.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France deeply regrets that this draft resolution was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The Council had before it a balanced, factual and focused text: it condemned the chemical weapons attack in Khan Shaykhun, demanded full cooperation with the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and insisted on immediate, safe and unhindered access to all relevant sites, including Shayrat airbase, and to all relevant information.

The use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. It cannot be treated with ambiguity or indifference. A clear majority of this Council supported the draft, and the failure to adopt it weakens the Council’s ability to uphold the chemical weapons prohibition and the obligations set out in resolution 2118 (2013).

France will not accept impunity. We will continue to work with our partners to ensure that the facts are established, that those responsible are held accountable, and that the Council does not remain silent in the face of such crimes. We call on the Syrian authorities to cooperate fully and unconditionally with the OPCW and the JIM, and on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and to allow immediate and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria.

France remains committed to a political solution under United Nations auspices in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). The Security Council must not abandon its responsibilities, and France will remain actively seized of this matter.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of this draft resolution because the reported use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun is a grave violation of international law and cannot be tolerated under any circumstances. Japan deeply regrets that the Security Council has been unable to adopt this resolution owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The Council must not remain silent when chemical weapons are used against civilians.

We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully with the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism and to provide immediate, safe and unhindered access to all relevant sites and information, including Shayrat airbase and records of air operations. Accountability must be pursued on the basis of an impartial, objective and transparent investigation. Japan also reiterates the need for immediate, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria and for all parties to respect international humanitarian law.

Japan reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and remains committed to a political solution under United Nations auspices. Japan will continue to work with all Council members to uphold the prohibition of chemical weapons and the unity of this Council.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation has voted against this draft resolution. We did not do so because we are indifferent to the loss of life in Khan Shaykhun or because we tolerate chemical weapons. The use of chemical weapons is unacceptable, and Russia has consistently supported an objective, impartial and professional investigation by the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism.

But the text before the Council was not an instrument for establishing the truth. From its very first operative paragraph it prejudged the outcome of an investigation that has not yet taken place. It made selective demands on the Syrian Government while imposing no equivalent requirements on armed groups and terrorist organizations. It included an unacceptable threat of sanctions, which would have turned the Security Council into an instrument of pressure and predetermined punishment. That is not a basis for Council unity; it is a formula for deepening confrontation.

We also cannot ignore that the draft said nothing about the unilateral missile strike by the United States against the Shayrat airbase, a flagrant violation of international law, the sovereignty of Syria and the Charter of the United Nations. The Council cannot demand respect for international law from one party while remaining silent when a permanent member acts unlawfully.

The Russian Federation remains committed to a genuine investigation of the Khan Shaykhun incident. We put forward balanced amendments that would have preserved the Council’s unity and focused it on the OPCW and the JIM rather than on pre-written conclusions. Those proposals were not accepted. We regret that our partners preferred a politicized text and a vote that could only divide the Council.

We reaffirm the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We call for an objective investigation that establishes the facts and identifies those responsible, not for a resolution that prejudges them. Russia will continue to work for a political settlement, for the fight against terrorism and for humanitarian access. We urge our colleagues to abandon the logic of confrontation and return to honest collective work on the basis of reliable facts and international law.
after.Senegal: Mr. President, Senegal takes the floor to express its deep regret that the Security Council was unable to adopt the draft resolution before it. The use of chemical weapons in Khan Shaykhun is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security, and it cannot remain without consequences. We voted in favour because we believe the Council must uphold the chemical weapons prohibition, demand full cooperation with the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism, and ensure accountability for those responsible. At the same time, we reiterate that the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria must be respected, and that there can be no military solution to this conflict. Senegal urges all parties to cooperate fully with the OPCW and the JIM, to grant immediate, safe and unhindered access, to protect civilians and humanitarian personnel, and to return to genuine intra-Syrian negotiations under United Nations auspices in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). The Council must remain united and actively seized of this matter.
after.Sweden:
Sweden voted in favour of this draft resolution because the use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and a threat to international peace and security. We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again been unable to speak with one voice in the face of such an attack. The reports from Khan Shaykhun are horrifying, and the victims and their families deserve accountability, not silence.

Sweden fully supports the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully and to provide immediate, safe and unhindered access to all relevant sites and information, including Shayrat airbase. The failure of the Council today does not absolve any party of its obligations under international law, including resolution 2118 and the Chemical Weapons Convention.

We also reiterate our call for full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria and for the protection of medical and humanitarian personnel and facilities. Sweden remains committed to a political solution through intra-Syrian negotiations under United Nations auspices, in accordance with resolution 2254. The Security Council must uphold the global prohibition against chemical weapons; today’s veto must not weaken that norm.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President, the United Kingdom is appalled that Russia has once again used its veto to prevent this Council from upholding the global prohibition on chemical weapons. This resolution was not about regime change. It was about a simple and fundamental principle: that chemical weapons must never be used, that the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism must have immediate, safe and unhindered access—including to Shayrat airbase and all relevant flight records—and that those responsible must be held accountable.

Russia’s veto does not erase the facts. It does not protect the Syrian people. It shields those who use chemical weapons from scrutiny. The images from Khan Shaykhun should have united this Council, not divided it. The United Kingdom voted in favour because we believe the Security Council must speak clearly against such atrocities. We regret that the Council has again failed to do so.

The Syrian regime remains bound by resolution 2118 and by the Chemical Weapons Convention. It must cooperate fully and immediately with the OPCW and the JIM. Russia must use its influence to ensure that happens. The United Kingdom will not abandon this issue or the Syrian people. We will continue to work with partners to preserve evidence, support a thorough and impartial investigation, and pursue accountability through all available means. This veto does not end the matter; it strengthens our resolve.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States is deeply disappointed and outraged by the Russian Federation’s veto of this necessary resolution. This text was not about sanctions, and it was not about regime change. It was a straightforward demand that the Syrian regime provide the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism with immediate, safe, and unhindered access to Shayrat airbase and all relevant information, including flight logs and records, so that the facts can be established and those responsible held accountable. By vetoing this resolution, Russia has chosen to protect a regime that has repeatedly used chemical weapons against its own people.

The images from Khan Shaykhun—children suffocating, families killed in their homes—are not fake. They are real, and this Council cannot pretend otherwise. The United States will not allow the use of chemical weapons to become normalized. The Council has failed to act today, but the United States will not be silent. We will continue to work with partners to preserve evidence, support an impartial investigation, and hold those responsible accountable. As we have demonstrated, the United States will act when chemical weapons are used and when our national security interests are threatened.

We remain committed to a political solution through the Geneva process, but there can be no impunity. We call on Russia to change course, to honor its commitments, and to stop shielding the Assad regime from accountability. The United States will continue to stand with the people of Syria and with all those who reject the use of chemical weapons.
after.Uruguay: Thank you, Mr. President. Uruguay voted in favour of this draft resolution because the use of chemical weapons is a grave violation of international law and cannot be met with indifference or impunity. My delegation regrets that the Security Council has once again been unable to adopt a text on such a crucial issue owing to the use of the veto. The prohibition of chemical weapons must be upheld without exception or political condition. We call on all parties, in particular the Syrian authorities, to cooperate fully with the OPCW and the Joint Investigative Mechanism and to provide immediate, safe and unhindered access to all relevant sites and information. Accountability and humanitarian access are essential, but they must also serve, not replace, the search for an inclusive political solution under United Nations auspices and in full respect for Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. Uruguay will continue to work for Council unity and for the protection of civilians.
